passages.note: Legislative digest for SB 101 (2015) describing its RFRA content and enactment; it does not name Clere's vote, so it is not his own act or words.
House 3rd-reading roll call on SB 101; Clere voted Nay, showing opposition to the RFRA's exemption but not which lower rung he holds.

passages.provision_quote: A governmental entity may substantially burden a person's exercise of religion only if the governmental entity demonstrates that application of the burden to the person: (1) is in furtherance of a compelling governmental interest; and (2) is the least restrictive means of furthering that compelling governmental interest.
passages.note: Enrolled act text of the bill Clere voted against; its compelling-interest/least-restrictive-means test is the annex's chair-shaped rung-4 instrument, but his Nay vote only shows opposition to it.

rows.reasoning: Clere voted Nay on SB 101 (2015), Indiana's RFRA, whose text bars government burdens on religious exercise unless a compelling interest is shown by the least restrictive means -- the annex's example of a rung-4 instrument ("protect religious freedom and allow faith-based exemptions ... unless compelling interest"). His No vote on this single-subject bill shows opposition to that broad exemption but, per V4.2, ruling out rung 4 is not evidence for which of rungs 1-3 he holds.
needs_source: Clere's own statement explaining his Nay vote on SB 101 (2015) (floor speech, press release, or similar), to show which of rungs 1-3 he holds on religious exemptions
